canonical_title: Opera introduces WebAI local inference browser API in Opera One early preview
aliases: Opera browser on-device AI WebAI standard
Opera One local model developer API
treatment: Repeat only for a published technical specification, independent cross-browser implementation, new stable API release, security model or measurable performance change.
known_facts: 2026-10-27 06:00 PDT (22:00 JST) TechCrunch reported Opera's new WebAI interface for running open-weight AI models directly inside the browser without cloud inference.
Opera One early preview is opt-in; Opera GX and Opera Neon support is announced as upcoming, not generally available.
Reported models include Google's Gemma and Apple's on-device foundation model on Macs; model support and performance are device-dependent.
WebAI is described as a proposed/new web standard by Opera and media, not verified as an adopted W3C standard; independent specification and interoperability evidence are pending.
Opera previously offered local LLM functionality in 2024; the hard delta is the new WebAI developer-facing interface and Opera One early preview, not the first-ever local AI capability.
reinclude_only_if: Opera publishes a formal WebAI specification, API reference, sample implementation or source code.
Other browsers or standards bodies independently adopt the interface.
Opera announces stable rollout, supported GPUs/models, permission/isolation or measurable resource usage.
notes: Primary new information is the 2026-10-27 WebAI early preview. Independent Opera technical specification URL was not confirmed at run time; 'standard' remains Opera's characterization.
